newsitem.title: USA: Mobil sees lower capital spending for '97.
newsitem.headline: Mobil sees lower capital spending for '97.

text.p: Total capital and exploration spending for 1997 is expected to be $5.4 billion, down from an estimated $7.0 billion spent in 1996, Mobil Corp said Friday in a statement.

Estimated 1996 spending was essentially equal to the amount budgeted for the year, the company said, noting that this amount excludes the nearly $2.0 billion spent for acquisitions of Ampolex Ltd and a 25 percent interest in the Tengiz oil field in Kazakhstan.
The 1997 spending budget can be revised if the business environment warrants changes, the company said.

Chairman Lucio Noto said the projected 1997 spending is consistent with Mobil's overall strategy to profitably grow its core businesses while continuing to improve the return on existing assets, adding that the expenditures will continue to be focused in the international area.

"The 1997 budget is close to 1996 expenditures adjusted for major acquisitions, and reflects Mobil's strong balance sheet and the continued redeployment of proceeds from the sale of assets which are non-core or worth more to others. In 1996, before tax proceeds from asset sales are estimated to have exceeded $1.5 billion." he added.
The company said worldwide exploration and production spending is expected to be about $3.5 billion in 1997, down from the $2.1 billion spent in 1996.

The program includes a diverse projects portfolio and aims to raise oil and natural gas production by an average of 3.5 percent a year through the early years of the next century, while replacing its reserve base by more than 100 percent annually, it said.
Mobil said U.S. exploration and producing spending is expected to be about $500 million, down about $100 million from 1996.
In the U.S., Mobil said it continues to focus on natural gas from Mobile Bay, heavy oil from California and light oil from projects in the Permian Basin.

In the international area, spending is expected to be about $3.0 billion, a decline of $1.3 billion from 1996, it said, including significant expenditures in West Africa, including Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea, as well as Kazakstan, Indonesia, Canada, Qatar, Norway and Venezuela.
It said exploration expense in 1997 is estimated to be in the range of $400-450 million compared with just over $500 million in 1996.

Refining and marketing spending for 1997 is projected to be about $1.3 billion, down about $1.O billion spent in 1996. The program focuses on profitable opportunities is such areas as the Asia Pacific, Latin America and Africa, as well as in the worldwide lubricants market, the company said.

Spending in U.S. marketing and refining is estimated to be about about $400 million, about the same as 1996, it said. A key U.S. program will be the roll-out of "On the Run" convenience stores, which will generate additional value from Mobil's retail sites, it said.

Spending in the international area is projected to be about $900 million, down about $300 million from 1996, Mobil said. Projects include a lube oil manufacturing facility at Mobil's Jurong refinery in Singapore, scheduled for start-up in the third quarter, lube blending facilities, including a new plant in China, and marketing opportunities in high growth markets.

Spending for Mobil Chemical is projected to be nearly $500 million, up about $100 million from 1996, it said, including expansions at olefins plant in Beaumont, Texas and a joint venture petrochemical complex in Saudi Arabia.
